meta.title: Your Houseplants Are Actually Listening to You #shorts
meta.description:
Have you ever talked to your plants? Well, science just proved they might actually be listening to you. Researchers recently discovered that flowers can hear the buzz of passing bees and will literally sweeten their nectar in response within minutes. But how? It turns out, the flower petals themselves act like microscopic ears, vibrating when sound waves of a specific frequency hit them. When a bee gets close, the flower senses the vibration and floods its sweet reward to attract the pollinator. If they can hear bees, what else are they listening to? Your music? Your private conversations? It makes you look at your garden in a completely different way. If you want to know more crazy secrets about the natural world, hit that follow button and tell me what you think your plants are overhearing!
